kurz: Seasoning to taste means asking what is missing and adjusting in a set order: salt first, then acid, then sweetness, heat and umami, fresh things last.
bild_im_kopf: Like tuning an instrument: the base note first, only then the fine strings.
was_passiert: Salt boosts all other tastes, so it comes first. Acid makes a dish lively and lighter. Sweetness, fat and umami round off and add depth. Herbs, lemon zest and pepper bring aroma that escapes in the heat, so they come last.
warum_wichtig: The step from following recipes to cooking for yourself: knowing how to season rescues bland, flat or overly hot dishes, even without a recipe.
faustregeln: Season in small steps and taste after each one: what is in cannot be taken out.
Unsure whether something fits: season just one spoonful first and compare.
Taste again after reducing, because salt concentrates as it does.
schritte: Taste at the temperature it will be served.
Bland, tastes of little: a pinch of salt, stir briefly, taste again.
Heavy, flat, tired: a few drops of lemon or vinegar.
Sharp, too sour or too hot: a little sweetness or fat, such as honey, butter or cream.
Lacks depth: umami, such as Parmesan, soy sauce, tomato paste or miso. At the very end herbs, lemon zest or pepper.
